<!--
  Thanks for contributing! Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a PR.

  Pull requests must be linked to an accepted issue. Every PR costs the
  maintainers a reproduction plus a verification of the fix; an issue lets us
  do the reproduction once and agree on the change before code is written.
  PRs that don't reference an accepted issue may be closed without review.

  Exception: trivial fixes (typos, broken links, comment-only changes) don't
  need an issue — replace the whole "Fixes #<issue-number>" line below with
  the single word "trivial".
-->

## Linked issue

<!-- Required. Use a closing keyword so GitHub links them, e.g. "Fixes #123". For an exempt change, replace the whole line with "trivial". -->

Fixes #<issue-number>

## Summary

<!-- What does this PR change, and why? Keep it to a few sentences; the detail belongs in the issue. -->

## How was this tested?

<!-- Steps a maintainer can follow to verify the fix, and which example/test app you used. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] The linked issue has been triaged and accepted by a maintainer (or this change is trivial)
- [ ] The change is scoped to what the issue describes; unrelated changes are in separate PRs
- [ ] Tests were added or updated where it makes sense
- [ ] A changeset was added (`pnpm changeset` in `js/`) if a published npm package changed
